title: Build production React TypeScript Vite dashboard application and asset pipeline
description:
Create the production React + TypeScript + Vite frontend project under dashboard/frontend with a reproducible, committed dependency lock. The deployed dashboard serves compiled assets from dashboard/frontend/dist through the FastAPI server from r.1. A Vite dev server must never be needed in deployment.

Before editing, inspect: mike_trade/dashboard/server.py and mike_trade/dashboard/api.py (from r.1) for the static dist directory location, the /api route prefix and the response models; the Makefile and CLI dashboard targets (if present) for the expected build/serve command names; and the repository docs on deployment.

Implement:
(1) dashboard/frontend/package.json:
- Pinned exact versions of react, react-dom, typescript, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react and @types/react / @types/react-dom.
- Scripts: build = 'tsc --noEmit && vite build', typecheck = 'tsc --noEmit', preview for local inspection only.
- private: true.
- An engines field for Node LTS.
- No charting-terminal libraries and no dependencies for notifications or analytics.
(2) dashboard/frontend/package-lock.json, generated by npm install from that package.json and committed (lockfileVersion 3).
(3) dashboard/frontend/tsconfig.json with strict mode, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, jsx react-jsx, moduleResolution bundler, include src.
(4) dashboard/frontend/vite.config.ts with the React plugin, base '/', build.outDir 'dist', emptyOutDir, hashed asset filenames, and sourcemap off by default. A dev-only server.proxy sends /api to the configured local FastAPI port and is documented as development-only.
(5) dashboard/frontend/index.html with a root div, a title 'mike_trade dashboard' and the module script /src/main.tsx. It has no inline mock data and no external CDN scripts.
(6) dashboard/frontend/src/main.tsx mounts <App /> imported from './App' into #root under React.StrictMode and imports './styles.css'.

App.tsx and styles.css are owned by r.3, so do not create them here. If they are absent, the full vite build is expected to succeed only after r.3/r.4 land, and the production build is confirmed in r.5. Bounded decision budget: do not add a router, state library or UI kit dependency. The plain React and fetch approach is sufficient.
acceptance_criteria: dashboard/frontend/package.json pins exact versions (no ^ or ~) of react, react-dom, typescript, vite and @vitejs/plugin-react, and defines build as 'tsc --noEmit && vite build' plus a typecheck script
dashboard/frontend/package-lock.json exists, is lockfileVersion 3, and is consistent with package.json (npm ci succeeds)
tsconfig.json enables strict mode and react-jsx
vite.config.ts outputs to dist with hashed asset names; any /api proxy is confined to the dev server config
index.html references only /src/main.tsx and contains no mock data, external CDN scripts or Vite dev-client references
main.tsx renders <App /> from './App' inside React.StrictMode into #root and imports './styles.css'
No file outside the allowed paths is created; App.tsx, styles.css, components and api client are not created by this task
forbidden_changes: replace React/TypeScript/Vite with server-rendered-only HTML, HTMX, a static mock or a notebook
make deployment depend on the Vite dev server
add charting-terminal, notification or analytics dependencies
add any UI control that places orders or mutates configuration
run broad test suites or backtests
